definitions.explanation: Indicates two actions happening simultaneously. The main action is in the second clause.
Expresses a concessive contrast, similar to のに but more formal. Often used in written language.

examples.japanese: ⟦{音楽|おんがく}→音楽：00661_ongaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}き→聞く：00483_kiku⟧ながら⟦{勉強|べんきょう}する→勉強する：00527_benkyousuru⟧。
examples.english: I study while listening to music.

examples.japanese: ⟦{歩|ある}き→歩く：00538_aruku⟧ながら⟦{話|はな}しましょう→話す：00467_hanasu⟧。

{朝|あさ}ごはん⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べ→食べる：00396_taberu⟧ながら⟦{新聞|しんぶん}→新聞：01440_shinbun⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}む→読む：00426_yomu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{習慣|しゅうかん}→習慣：01429_shuukan⟧です。
examples.english: Reading the newspaper while eating breakfast is my daily habit.

examples.japanese: ⟦{知|し}ってい→知る：00458_shiru⟧ながら⟦{教|おし}えて→教える：00526_oshieru⟧⟦くれなかった→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
examples.english: Although they knew, they didn't tell me.

examples.japanese: ⟦{残念|ざんねん}→残念：01244_zannen⟧ながら、⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{参加|さんか}→参加：02498_sanka⟧⟦できません→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: Unfortunately, I cannot attend on that day.

notes:
ながら has two main uses: simultaneous actions and concessive contrast.

SIMULTANEOUS ACTIONS (sense 1):
- Attach to the verb stem (ます-form without ます)
- The subject of both clauses must be the same person
- The main action is the second clause; ながら marks the secondary action
- Example: ⟦{食|た}べ→食べる：00396_taberu⟧ながら⟦{話|はな}す→話す：00467_hanasu⟧ (talk while eating — talking is the main action)

CONCESSIVE USE (sense 2):
- More formal and literary than ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ or けど
- Common set phrases: ⟦{残念|ざんねん}→残念：01244_zannen⟧ながら (unfortunately), ⟦{少|すく}ない→少ない：01136_sukunai⟧ながら (though few)

WATCH OUT:
- ながら requires the same subject in both clauses. Use ⟦{間|あいだ}→間：00914_aida⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ when the subjects differ.
